title: Rape
old_text: A man is said to commit rape who penetrates his penis into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so; or inserts any object or body part; or manipulates any body part; or applies his mouth to the vagina, anus, or urethra, under circumstances including against her will, without her consent, with consent obtained by putting her in fear of death or hurt, or when she is under 18 years of age.
new_text: A man is said to commit rape if he penetrates his penis into the vagina, urethra, or anus of a woman or makes her do so; or inserts any object or body part not being the penis; or manipulates any body part to cause penetration; or applies his mouth to sexual organs, without consent or under statutory disqualifications (including fear of death/hurt, false belief of marriage, intoxication, unsound mind, or woman under 18 years).
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 376.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 64.
explanation: Defines the offence of rape, retaining the expansive four-clause definition introduced post-2013 while placing Offences Against Women and Children prominently at the front of the code in Chapter V. The age of consent is maintained at 18 years.

title: Punishment for rape
old_text: Whoever commits rape shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine; aggravated categories under subsection (2) carried minimums of ten years up to natural life.
new_text: Whoever commits rape shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine (sub-section 1); aggravated rape by police officers, public servants, armed forces, or in custody carries minimum 10 years up to natural life (sub-section 2).
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years up to life, and fine; aggravated rape min 10 years to natural life.
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years up to life, and fine; aggravated rape min 10 years to natural life; fine directed to victim's medical expenses and rehabilitation.
explanation: Provides mandatory baseline sentencing for rape and aggravated custodial rape. Specifically mandates that fines collected shall be just and reasonable to cover the victim's medical expenses and rehabilitation.

title: Punishment for rape in certain cases
old_text: IPC Section 376(3) punished rape on a woman under 16 years with rigorous imprisonment not less than 20 years up to life; IPC Section 376AB punished rape on a woman under 12 years with rigorous imprisonment not less than 20 years up to natural life, or death.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever commits rape on a woman under sixteen years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for not less than twenty years up to life (remainder of natural life) and fine. Sub-section (2): Whoever commits rape on a woman under twelve years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than twenty years up to natural life, or death.
punishment_old: Under 16: min 20 years to natural life; Under 12: min 20 years to natural life or death.
punishment_new: Under 16 (65(1)): min 20 years to natural life and fine; Under 12 (65(2)): min 20 years to natural life or death, with fine payable to victim.
explanation: Consolidates special child rape provisions (former IPC 376(3) and 376AB) into a single structured section with two severity tiers. Retains capital punishment for rape of girls under twelve years of age.

title: Punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim
old_text: Whoever commits an offence punishable under section 376 and in the course of such commission inflicts an injury which causes the death of the woman or causes the woman to be in a persistent vegetative state, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than twenty years up to natural life, or with death.
new_text: Whoever commits an offence punishable under sub-section (1) or (2) of section 64 and in the course of such commission inflicts an injury which causes the death of the woman or causes her to be in a persistent vegetative state, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for not less than twenty years up to natural life, or with death.
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 20 years up to natural life, or with death.
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 20 years up to natural life, or with death.
explanation: Mandates life imprisonment (remainder of natural life) or the death penalty where rape results in death or a persistent vegetative state. Renumbered from IPC Section 376A without diluting penalty.

title: Sexual intercourse by husband upon his wife during separation
old_text: Whoever has sexual intercourse with his own wife, who is living separately from him under a decree of separation or under any custom or usage, without her consent, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than two years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Whoever has sexual intercourse with his own wife, who is living separately from him under a decree of separation or under any custom or usage, without her consent, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than two years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment not less than 2 years but which may extend to 7 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment not less than 2 years but which may extend to 7 years, and fine.
explanation: Punishes non-consensual sexual intercourse by a husband upon his separated wife during a decree of separation or customary separation. Renumbered from IPC Section 376B.

title: Sexual intercourse by a person in authority
old_text: Whoever, being in a position of authority or in a fiduciary relationship, or being a public servant, or superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home or women's or children's institution, or hospital, abuses such authority or position to induce or seduce any woman to have sexual intercourse, shall be punished.
new_text: Whoever, being in a position of authority or in a fiduciary relationship, or being a public servant, or superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home or other place of custody, or hospital, abuses such authority or position to induce or seduce any woman in his custody or care to have sexual intercourse (not amounting to rape), shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment.
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 5 years but which may extend to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 5 years but which may extend to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Penalizes custodial and fiduciary sexual exploitation where consent is vitiated through official power, hierarchical domination, or institutional oversight. Renumbered from IPC Section 376C with clarified language.

title: Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means, etc.
old_text: None (No standalone section in IPC; prosecuted under IPC Section 375/90 as rape under misconception of fact or under IPC Section 417 for cheating).
new_text: Whoever, by deceitful means or by making a promise to marry a woman without any intention of fulfilling the same, and has sexual intercourse with her, such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Deceitful means include the false promise of employment or promotion, or marrying after suppressing identity.
punishment_old: Not codified as a distinct penal offence; litigated under rape (IPC 375/376) or cheating (IPC 417).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: A major statutory innovation in the BNS addressing false promises of marriage and deceitful identity manipulation. It separates consensual relationships founded on bad-faith promises or disguised religious/personal identity from traditional violent rape, prescribing a targeted maximum penalty of ten years.

title: Gang rape
old_text: IPC Section 376D punished gang rape with rigorous imprisonment not less than 20 years up to natural life; IPC Section 376DA punished gang rape of girl under 16 with natural life; IPC Section 376DB punished gang rape of girl under 12 with natural life or death.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Where a woman is raped by one or more persons acting in furtherance of a common intention, each person is deemed guilty of gang rape and punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than twenty years up to life (natural life) and fine. Sub-section (2): Where a woman under eighteen years of age is gang raped, each person shall be punished with imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life) and fine, or with death.
punishment_old: General: min 20 years to natural life; Under 16: natural life; Under 12: natural life or death.
punishment_new: General (70(1)): min 20 years to natural life and fine; Minor under 18 (70(2)): imprisonment for remainder of natural life and fine, or death.
explanation: Merges disparate IPC gang rape provisions into two cohesive tiers. Significantly, Section 70(2) expands capital punishment / natural life imprisonment to cover the gang rape of any minor female under eighteen years of age (raising the threshold from 12/16 under former IPC sections).

title: Punishment for repeat offenders
old_text: Whoever has been previously convicted of an offence punishable under section 376, 376A, 376AB, 376D, 376DA or 376DB and is subsequently convicted of an offence punishable under any of the said sections shall be punished with imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life) or with death.
new_text: Whoever has been previously convicted of an offence punishable under section 64, 65, 66, or 70 and is subsequently convicted of an offence punishable under any of the said sections shall be punished with imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, or with death.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for remainder of natural life, or death.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for remainder of natural life, or death.
explanation: Imposes mandatory life imprisonment (natural life) or capital punishment for habitual or recidivist offenders convicted of multiple severe sexual offences. Renumbered from IPC Section 376E.

title: Disclosure of identity of victim of certain offences, etc.
old_text: Whoever prints or publishes the name or any matter which may make known the identity of any person against whom an offence under section 376, 376A, 376B, 376C, 376D or 376E is alleged or found to have been committed shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years and fine.
new_text: Whoever prints or publishes the name or any matter which may make known the identity of any person against whom an offence under section 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70 or 71 is alleged or found to have been committed shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years and fine.
explanation: Strictly prohibits disclosing the identity of victims of sexual crimes, shielding privacy and protecting dignity. Renumbered from IPC Section 228A and moved into Chapter V.

title: Printing or publishing any matter relating to court proceedings without permission
old_text: IPC Section 228A(3) penalized printing or publishing any matter in relation to in-camera judicial proceedings with respect to sexual offences without previous permission of the court.
new_text: Whoever prints or publishes any matter in relation to any proceeding before a court with respect to an offence referred to in section 72 without previous permission of such court shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years and fine under IPC Section 228A(3).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years and fine.
explanation: Carved out from IPC Section 228A(3) into a dedicated standalone section penalizing unauthorized publication of in-camera or sensitive court proceedings relating to sexual assault cases.

title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
old_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment not less than 1 year up to 5 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment not less than 1 year up to 5 years, and fine.
explanation: Penalizes physical assault or criminal force targeted against a woman with intent to outrage her modesty. Renumbered from IPC Section 354.

title: Sexual harassment
old_text: A man committing physical contact and advances involving unwelcome sexual overtures; demand or request for sexual favours; showing pornography against a woman's will; or making sexually coloured remarks shall be guilty of sexual harassment.
new_text: A man committing physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; a demand or request for sexual favours; showing pornography against the will of a woman; or making sexually coloured remarks shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment.
punishment_old: Physical contact / demand / pornography: rigorous imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both; sexually coloured remarks: imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both.
punishment_new: Physical contact / demand / pornography: rigorous imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both; sexually coloured remarks: imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both.
explanation: Defines and punishes the four statutory forms of sexual harassment. Retains the two sentencing categories from IPC Section 354A.

title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to disrobe
old_text: Any man who assaults or uses criminal force to any woman or abets such act with the intention of disrobing or compelling her to be naked, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Any man who assaults or uses criminal force to any woman or abets such act with the intention of disrobing or compelling her to be naked, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment not less than 3 years but which may extend to 7 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment not less than 3 years but which may extend to 7 years, and fine.
explanation: Criminalizes acts of stripping, disrobing, or compelling a woman to be naked in public or private. Renumbered from IPC Section 354B.

title: Voyeurism
old_text: Any man who watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually expect not being observed, or disseminates such image, shall be punished.
new_text: Any man who watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually expect not being observed, or disseminates such image, shall be punished.
punishment_old: First conviction: imprisonment 1 to 3 years and fine; second or subsequent conviction: imprisonment 3 to 7 years and fine.
punishment_new: First conviction: imprisonment 1 to 3 years and fine; second or subsequent conviction: imprisonment 3 to 7 years and fine.
explanation: Penalizes surreptitious recording, surveillance, or digital distribution of intimate private acts where privacy is reasonably expected. Renumbered from IPC Section 354C.

title: Stalking
old_text: Any man who follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest; or monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking.
new_text: Any man who follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest; or monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking.
punishment_old: First conviction: imprisonment up to 3 years and fine; second or subsequent conviction: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine.
punishment_new: First conviction: imprisonment up to 3 years and fine; second or subsequent conviction: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine.
explanation: Covers physical following as well as cyberstalking and online surveillance of a woman despite expressed disinterest. Renumbered from IPC Section 354D.

title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman
old_text: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any word, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to three years, and with fine.
new_text: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any words, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object in any form, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to 3 years, and with fine.
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to 3 years, and with fine.
explanation: Penalizes verbal abuse, obscene gestures, lewd gestures, and intrusions upon privacy intended to insult female modesty. Renumbered from IPC Section 509 and moved into Chapter V.

title: Dowry death
old_text: Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called dowry death.
new_text: Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called dowry death.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than 7 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than 7 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life.
explanation: Maintains the 7-year statutory window and cruelty presumption for dowry deaths. Renumbered from IPC Section 304B directly into Chapter V under marriage-related offences.

title: Cohabitation caused by a man deceitfully inducing a belief of lawful marriage
old_text: Every man who by deceit causes any woman who is not lawfully married to him to believe that she is lawfully married to him and to cohabit or have sexual intercourse with him in that belief, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Every man who by deceit causes any woman who is not lawfully married to him to believe that she is lawfully married to him and to cohabit or have sexual intercourse with him in that belief, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Penalizes deceitfully misleading a woman into believing she is legally married so as to induce cohabitation or sexual relations. Renumbered from IPC Section 493.

title: Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife
old_text: IPC Section 494 punished bigamy with imprisonment up to 7 years and fine; IPC Section 495 punished bigamy with concealment of former marriage with imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever marries having a husband or wife living, where such marriage is void by reason of taking place during the life of such spouse, shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years and fine. Sub-section (2): Whoever commits the offence under sub-section (1) having concealed from the person with whom subsequent marriage is contracted the fact of the former marriage, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
punishment_old: Standard bigamy (IPC 494): up to 7 years and fine; with concealment (IPC 495): up to 10 years and fine.
punishment_new: Standard bigamy (82(1)): imprisonment up to 7 years and fine; with concealment (82(2)): imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.
explanation: Merges IPC Sections 494 and 495 into a single cohesive bigamy section with two subsections distinguishing open bigamous remarriage from fraudulent bigamy involving concealment.

title: Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage
old_text: Whoever, dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention, goes through the ceremony of being married, knowing that he is not thereby lawfully married, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Whoever, dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention, goes through the ceremony of being married, knowing that he is not thereby lawfully married, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 7 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 7 years, and fine.
explanation: Penalizes mock, bogus, or legally invalid marriage ceremonies performed dishonestly with fraudulent intent. Renumbered from IPC Section 496.

title: Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman
old_text: Whoever takes or entices away any woman who is and whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the wife of any other man, from that man, or from any person having the care of her on behalf of that man, with intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person, or conceals or detains with that intent any such woman, shall be punished.
new_text: Whoever takes or entices away any woman who is and whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the wife of any other man, with intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person, or conceals or detains with that intent any such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both.
explanation: Penalizes enticing, abducting, or detaining a married woman for the purpose of illicit intercourse. Renumbered from IPC Section 498.

title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
old_text: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine (with definition of cruelty embedded in the explanation).
new_text: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 3 years and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 3 years and fine.
explanation: Preserves the criminal sanction against matrimonial cruelty by a husband or his relatives. In the BNS, the substantive offence is codified in Section 85, while the definition of cruelty is split into dedicated Section 86.

title: Cruelty defined
old_text: In IPC Section 498A, cruelty was defined in an appended Explanation covering wilful conduct likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment to coerce unlawful property demands.
new_text: For the purposes of section 85, cruelty means: (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical); or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security.
punishment_old: Definition clause forming part of IPC Section 498A.
punishment_new: Definitional provision governing Section 85.
explanation: Elevates the Explanation clause of former IPC Section 498A into a dedicated statutory section defining both physical/mental cruelty and unlawful dowry coercion.

title: Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc.
old_text: Whoever kidnaps or abducts any woman with intent that she may be compelled, or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled, to marry any person against her will, or in order that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
new_text: Whoever kidnaps or abducts any woman with intent that she may be compelled, or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled, to marry any person against her will, or in order that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years and fine.
explanation: Penalizes kidnapping or abduction executed to coerce a woman into involuntary marriage or forced sexual intercourse. Renumbered from IPC Section 366.

title: Causing miscarriage
old_text: Whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry, shall, if such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman, be punished with imprisonment up to three years or fine or both; and if the woman be quick with child, with imprisonment up to seven years and fine.
new_text: Whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry, shall, if such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and if the woman be quick with child, with imprisonment up to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both; if woman is quick with child, up to 7 years and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both; if woman is quick with child, up to 7 years and fine.
explanation: Criminalizes non-therapeutic miscarriage not performed in good faith to save the mother's life. Renumbered from IPC Section 312.

title: Causing miscarriage without woman's consent
old_text: Whoever commits the offence defined in the last preceding section without the consent of the woman, whether the woman is quick with child or not, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Whoever commits the offence defined in section 88 without the consent of the woman, whether the woman is quick with child or not, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Penalizes forcing or administering an abortion upon a woman without her free consent, subjecting the offender to life imprisonment. Renumbered from IPC Section 313.

title: Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage
old_text: Whoever, with intent to cause the miscarriage of a woman with child, does any act which causes the death of such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and fine; and if done without the consent of the woman, with imprisonment for life or up to ten years.
new_text: Whoever, with intent to cause the miscarriage of a woman with child, does any act which causes the death of such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the act is done without the consent of the woman, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with the punishment above mentioned.
punishment_old: With consent: imprisonment up to 10 years and fine; without consent: imprisonment for life, or up to 10 years and fine.
punishment_new: With consent: imprisonment up to 10 years and fine; without consent: imprisonment for life, or up to 10 years and fine.
explanation: Imposes severe punishment when an illegal abortion causes the death of the pregnant mother, with life imprisonment mandated if performed without her consent. Renumbered from IPC Section 314.

title: Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause it to die after birth
old_text: Whoever before the birth of any child does any act with the intention of thereby preventing that child from being born alive or causing it to die after its birth, and does by such act prevent that child from being born alive, or causes it to die after its birth, shall, if such act be not caused in good faith for saving the life of the mother, be punished with imprisonment up to ten years, or fine, or both.
new_text: Whoever before the birth of any child does any act with the intention of thereby preventing that child from being born alive or causing it to die after its birth, and does by such act prevent that child from being born alive, or causes it to die after its birth, shall, if such act be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the mother, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, or with fine, or with both.
explanation: Protects unborn infants from acts intended to prevent live birth or cause neonatal death, with exceptions strictly limited to bona fide maternal lifesaving interventions. Renumbered from IPC Section 315.

title: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide
old_text: Whoever does any act under such circumstances, that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide, and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Whoever does any act under such circumstances, that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide, and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Punishes acts that would amount to culpable homicide if the mother died, where the act instead terminates the life of a quick unborn foetus. Renumbered from IPC Section 316.

title: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years by parent or person having care of it
old_text: Whoever being the father or mother of a child under the age of twelve years, or having the care of such child, shall expose or leave such child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning such child, shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both.
new_text: Whoever being the father or mother of a child under the age of twelve years, or having the care of such child, shall expose or leave such child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 7 years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 7 years, or with fine, or with both.
explanation: Penalizes parents or guardians who desert or expose children under twelve years of age with intent to abandon them completely. Renumbered from IPC Section 317.

title: Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body
old_text: Whoever, by secretly burying or otherwise disposing of the dead body of a child whether such child died before or after or during its birth, intentionally conceals or endeavours to conceal the birth of such child, shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
new_text: Whoever, by secretly burying or otherwise disposing of the dead body of a child whether such child died before or after or during its birth, intentionally conceals or endeavours to conceal the birth of such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both.
explanation: Penalizes secret disposal or burial of a deceased infant's body with the intent to hide its birth. Renumbered from IPC Section 318.

title: Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence
old_text: None (Under IPC, adults exploiting children were charged as abettors or under special acts like Juvenile Justice Act, with no specific penal code provision for child deployment in crime).
new_text: Whoever hires, employs or engages any child to commit an offence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to ten years, and with fine; and if the offence be committed shall also be punished with the punishment provided for that offence as if the offence has been committed by such person himself. Hiring or engaging a child for sexual exploitation or pornography is expressly covered.
punishment_old: Not specifically codified in IPC as a standalone offence.
punishment_new: Rigorous/simple imprisonment not less than 3 years but up to 10 years and fine; plus punishment for the substantive offence as if committed by the adult himself.
explanation: A pioneering child protection provision introduced in the BNS directly criminalizing adults who hire, engage, or exploit children to execute crimes or engage in sexual exploitation/child pornography. The adult faces severe minimum sentences and double liability as the principal offender.

title: Procuration of child
old_text: Whoever, by any means whatsoever, induces any minor girl under the age of eighteen years to go from any place or to do any act with intent that such girl may be, or knowing that it is likely that she will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person, shall be punishable with imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
new_text: Whoever, by any means whatsoever, induces any child to go from any place or to do any act with intent that such child may be, or knowing that it is likely that such child will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person, shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.
explanation: Modifies former IPC Section 366A by replacing gender-restricted 'minor girl' with the gender-neutral term 'child' (under eighteen years of age), providing universal protection to all minors against sexual procuration.

title: Importation of child from foreign country
old_text: Whoever imports into India from any country outside India any girl under the age of twenty-one years with intent that she may be, or knowing it to be likely that she will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person, shall be punishable with imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
new_text: Whoever imports into India from any country outside India or from the State of Jammu and Kashmir any child under the age of eighteen years with intent that such child may be, or knowing it to be likely that such child will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person, shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine (applied to girl under 21).
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine (standardized to child under 18 years).
explanation: Standardizes the age threshold to 'child' (under eighteen years of age) and extends gender-neutral coverage against international trafficking for sexual exploitation. Modified from IPC Section 366B.

title: Selling child for purposes of prostitution, etc.
old_text: Whoever sells, lets to hire, or otherwise disposes of any person under the age of eighteen years with intent that such person shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
new_text: Whoever sells, lets to hire, or otherwise disposes of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Penalizes selling or hiring children for prostitution or immoral exploitation, with statutory presumptions regarding possession. Modified from IPC Section 372 using unified 'child' nomenclature.

title: Buying child for purposes of prostitution, etc.
old_text: Whoever buys, hires or otherwise obtains possession of any person under the age of eighteen years with intent that such person shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
new_text: Whoever buys, hires or otherwise obtains possession of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Penalizes purchasing, hiring, or taking custody of any child for prostitution or unlawful sexual exploitation, maintaining strict presumptions against brothel keepers. Modified from IPC Section 373.
